column1: Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga suki desu.,I like driving.,わたしはくるまをうんてんするのがすきです,sentence,,わたし
column10: です,,"Unten suru means drive. Suru stays in dictionary form before no. Suki is a na-adjective, not a verb."

column1: Watashi wa itsumo kuruma o unten shimasu.,I always drive.,わたしはいつもくるまをうんてんします,sentence,,わたし
column7: します,,Unten suru → unten shimasu: polite nonpast. Itsumo means always.

column1: Unten wa tanoshikute omoshiroi to omoimasu.,I think driving is fun and interesting.,うんてんはたのしくておもしろいとおもいます,sentence,,うんてん
column6: おもいます,,Tanoshii → tanoshikute links two descriptions. Omou → omoimasu means think (polite).

column1: Watashi wa shashin o toru no ga kirai desu. Muzukashii kara desu.,I dislike taking photos because it’s difficult.,わたしはしゃしんをとるのがきらいですむずかしいからです,sentence,,わたし
column12: です,,Toru (u-verb) means take a photo; it stays in dictionary form before no. Kirai is a na-adjective. Muzukashii is an i-adjective.

column1: Sorekara, watashi wa ryouri o suru no ga jouzu desu. Omoshiroi to omou kara desu.,"Then, I’m good at cooking because I find it interesting.",それからわたしはりょうりをするのがじょうずですおもしろいとおもうからです,sentence,,それから
column15: です,,"Suru stays in dictionary form before no. Jouzu is a na-adjective. Omou stays plain before kara, even though the sentence ends politely."

column1: Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga heta desu. Amari renshuu shinai kara desu.,I’m bad at sports because I don’t practice much.,わたしはスポーツをするのがへたですあまりれんしゅうしないからです,sentence,,わたし
column14: です,,Suru stays unchanged before no. Renshuu suru → renshuu shinai is the plain negative of practice. Heta is a na-adjective.

column1: Motto renshuu shimasu.,I will practice more.,もっとれんしゅうします,sentence,,もっと
column3: します,,Renshuu suru → renshuu shimasu. Polite nonpast can express future intention; motto means more.
